question: Does the SLHA compressed-score quality gap come from key-RANKING errors or from order-preserving errors in the score gaps/shape?
diagnostic_only_warning: These oracles require access to exact baseline scores and are not deployable replacement methods. They are measurement instruments: default-off, and every one of them reads the baseline Q·K row that a compressed KV cache exists to avoid computing.

top16_vs_full_oracle_A_screening_differe.statement: The top-16 and full-ranking screening values differ by 0.0113 PPL, which is small relative to the coarse four-chunk screening protocol. The twelve-chunk validation is used to determine whether this difference persists.
top16_vs_full_oracle_A_screening_differe.outcome: It did not persist with the same sign: at twelve chunks top-16 sits 0.0522 PPL ABOVE full ranking rather than below it. Top-16 still reaches 98.42% of the full Oracle A recovery, so approximate saturation holds, but the four-chunk contrast was too fine for its sign to be meaningful.

counter_comparisons.note: NOT required to be equal: the pass-through control selects no layer, so the replace path never runs and every strict counter is legitimately zero, whereas the baseline-identity oracle exercises the full replace path. These two are compared on PPL, which must match exactly.

identity_controls.gating_note: E, F, G, H and I are not interpreted unless both identity controls are exact. Any identity mismatch invalidates the causal interpretation.
identity_controls.passthrough_note: the pass-through control selects no layer, so the replace path never runs and its strict counters are legitimately zero. It is compared against the baseline-identity oracle on PPL, not on counters.

oracle_B_slha_rank_visible_baseline_valu.interpretation: Applying the baseline value distribution to the incorrect SLHA key ordering amplifies the quality loss. This demonstrates a strong interaction between key assignment and score geometry; it does not prove that score geometry is irrelevant.

primary_oracles.additivity_note: Oracle A and Oracle B are reported independently. They are NOT an additive decomposition, their fractions do not sum to 1, and they must not be read as a variance partition.

nine_configuration_matrix.identity_method: compared on the full parsed numeric representation (repr of the parsed float) and on the sha256 of the raw summary content; no rounded display value is used to verify identity

topk_saturation.screening_claim: screening suggested that top-1 captures a large fraction of the available ranking benefit and that top-16 is approximately saturated relative to full ranking
topk_saturation.verdict_top1: CONFIRMED: top-1 restoration alone reaches 79.93% of the full Oracle A recovery
topk_saturation.verdict_top16: CONFIRMED as approximate saturation: top-16 reaches 98.42% of the full Oracle A recovery
topk_saturation.sign_change_note: The SIGN of the top-16 minus full-ranking difference reversed between the two resolutions. At four chunks top-16 was 0.0113 PPL BELOW full ranking; at twelve chunks it is 0.0522 PPL ABOVE it. The screening appearance that top-16 slightly exceeded full ranking therefore does NOT persist: at the validated resolution top-16 recovers slightly less than the full ranking, as expected. Both differences are small in absolute terms, but the reversal is why the four-chunk contrast was never promoted to a claim.

early_layer_final.explanation: Correcting rankings only in early layers can outperform correcting every layer because some later-layer SLHA deviations may be compensating, while early ranking errors trigger downstream amplification. This does not mean later layers are irrelevant.

V_F_rankB.description: Oracle B: SLHA ranking, visible baseline values

conclusion.statement:
Restoring the baseline ordering of causally visible keys while preserving the causally visible SLHA score-value multiset recovered most of the measured quality gap. Correcting only a small number of highest-ranked keys captured a large fraction of that benefit, and correcting layers 0-6 prevented substantial downstream amplification.

The dominant measured mechanism is therefore incorrect assignment of high score values to visible keys. A substantial order-preserving residual remains, and Oracle B demonstrates that key assignment and score geometry interact strongly.
explicitly_not_claimed: the residual is purely magnitude error
Oracle A and Oracle B partition the gap additively
conclusion.deployability: These oracles require access to exact baseline scores and are not deployable replacement methods. Every oracle in this experiment reads the baseline Q·K row that a compressed KV cache exists precisely to avoid computing; the measurements bound what a better codec could achieve, they do not constitute one.
limitations: one model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q8_0), one corpus (WikiText-2 raw test), one codec configuration; nothing here is shown to generalise
twelve chunks of 512 tokens is 6144 tokens -- enough to separate these effects, far short of a full benchmark
the layerwise decomposition and the early-layer interaction are FOUR-CHUNK screening results; no twelve-chunk layerwise matrix was run
the active-key statistics come from a deterministic 1-in-16 token, 2-of-12 head sample, not an exhaustive pass
perplexity is the only quality metric; no downstream task was measured
the order-preserving residual is quantified but not explained -- this experiment does not identify what it consists of
two process-tree terminations remain unexplained; they were reconciled by re-running, not by root-cause analysis
conclusion.recommended_next_experiment: Constrain the codec so that the top-k baseline ordering is preserved by construction and measure how much of the 65.92% ranking recovery survives without any baseline-score access. The top-1 result (79.93% of the full ranking benefit from a single key) and the layers 0-6 result (87.80% of the gap from seven layers) together suggest the cheapest viable target: an early-layer, top-k-preserving score path. A parallel line should attack the order-preserving residual directly, since PR #62 already ruled out a per-row rescaling constant and this experiment shows the residual is 34.08% of the gap even with the ranking exactly correct.

classification_precedence: unstable_denominator: |damage| < eps -- checked first, because every fraction below is undefined when the denominator is not resolvable
negative_damage: damage <= -eps -- replacing this layer alone IMPROVES PPL, so a 'recovered fraction' has no meaning regardless of the oracle change
over_recovery: damage >= eps and oracle_change > damage (fraction > 1) -- the oracle drives PPL below pass-through; the fraction is reported uncapped
negative_recovery: damage >= eps and oracle_change < 0 -- the transplant makes this layer worse; the negative fraction is reported signed, never clipped

layer_5.finding: layer 5 has the LARGEST single-layer damage (0.5578 PPL) and the largest absolute oracle recovery (0.4220 PPL), but its absolute recovery does NOT exceed its damage: the recovered fraction is 0.7565 and the oracle result 9.5210 remains ABOVE pass-through 9.3852. Layer 5 is therefore positive_recovery, not over_recovery.

over_recovery_check.note: no screening layer recovers more than 100%. The three layers whose oracle PPL falls below pass-through are 3, 10 and 25, which are exactly the negative-damage and unstable-denominator layers where the fraction is undefined by the declared precedence rules. No fraction is capped anywhere in this report.

active_key_metrics.domain: causally visible keys only (written, in-stream, finite, unmasked)
active_key_metrics.supersedes: the PR #60 top-1/top-5 figures, which were computed over the full padded row including causally masked keys
active_key_metrics.aggregation_warning: micro and macro figures answer different questions and are never averaged together or reported unlabelled

micro.definition: weighted over all valid sampled rows/pairs, layers pooled
micro.boundary_tie_note: the k-th and (k+1)-th baseline scores are exactly equal, so which key is 'in' the top k is decided by the deterministic index tiebreak rather than by the score

tie_count_scope.warning: these tie counts are NOT comparable with the exhaustive oracle counter oracle_ties (12511 on the full-model Oracle A run). The oracle counter is exhaustive over every replaced vector and counts tied comparisons encountered during permutation construction; the figures here are exact-equality pair counts over a deterministic 1-in-16 token, 2-of-12 head sample of rows. Different populations and different definitions -- do not divide one by the other.

accounting.identity: physical == included + causally_masked + padding + inactive_stream + nonfinite, checked on every sampled row
